method: Full-system PANDA (QEMU) + taint2 byte-precise dynamic taint; 80 stdin-derived register bytes labeled at nft_byteorder_eval entry, taint queried on every guest write into canary_after
notes: taint2 observed 20 out-of-bounds writes into canary_after (single store PC 0x4034ca, stride 4, all writing 0xefcd) -- the exact 20-write overshoot geometry. NONE carried attacker taint on the stored VALUE: the overshoot (loop iterations 20..39) reads the sentinel region's own constants, not stdin, so byte-precise data-flow correctly reports the values as clean. Sanity: 20/20 in-bounds byteswap writes into the register file ARE tainted, proving taint2 propagates through ntohs/htons -- the OOB 'clean' result is a true data-flow fact, not an engine miss. This is where taint2 (pure value data-flow) diverges from microtaint's shadow, which reports the same 20 writes as tainted.
